samples.text:
The maps show a housing estate in 1970 and after it was regenerated in 2020. Overall, the estate became more greener and has more facilities for the people, but the two main roads, terraced houses and shops are same.

In 1970, Ring Road and Oak Avenue crossed in the middle of the estate. There was tower blocks in the north-west and terraced houses in the north-east, with open grassland behind them. In the south-west there were garages and a car park, and in the south there were shops and a waste ground.

In 2020, the tower blocks have been replaced by low-rise flats and houses. The open grassland is now a park and a play area. In the south-west, the garages were removed and there is a smaller car park, a community centre and allotments. Also, a medical centre was built on the waste ground and some trees was planted next to it. The terraced houses and the shops did not change.
samples.why: Overview present · key changes covered in a mostly list-like way · basic linking · adequate vocabulary · errors in comparative form, agreement and articles that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate a housing estate in 1970 and the same estate following its regeneration in 2020. Overall, the estate has been transformed into a more varied and community-focused neighbourhood, with high-rise housing and unused land replaced by lower buildings, services and green spaces, while the road layout has been retained.

In both years, Ring Road runs from west to east and crosses Oak Avenue in the centre of the estate. North of Ring Road, the tower blocks in the north-west have been demolished and replaced by low-rise flats and houses. The terraced houses in the north-east have been kept, but the open grassland behind them has been divided into a park and a play area.

South of Ring Road, the garages and car park which took up the whole south-west have been reduced to a smaller car park, next to which a community centre has been built, with allotments to the north of both. The shops remain in the same place, whereas the waste ground in the south-east have been developed into a medical centre and an area of trees.
samples.why: Clear overview · changes logically divided by Ring Road · good cohesion and referencing · appropriate vocabulary (regeneration, community-focused) · mostly error-free with a minor agreement slip.

samples.text:
The maps depict a housing estate in 1970 and after its regeneration in 2020. The overarching change is a move away from high-rise blocks and neglected land towards lower-density housing, community services and landscaped green space, all within an unchanged street pattern.

The estate is still divided into quarters by Ring Road, running east to west, and Oak Avenue, running north to south. In the north-west, the tower blocks have been cleared and replaced by low-rise flats on the western side and houses to their east. Across Oak Avenue, the terraced houses remain, but the open grassland behind them has been landscaped into a park with a play area at its eastern end.

South of Ring Road, the garages and car park that once filled the south-western quarter have been scaled down to a single car park, and the land released now accommodates a community centre and, to their north, a strip of allotments. The shops beside Oak Avenue have been retained, while the former waste ground in the south-east has been put to use, with a medical centre in its southern part and a cluster of trees to the north.
samples.why: Perceptive overview · features precisely compared quarter by quarter · cohesion natural and effective · sophisticated, precise vocabulary (lower-density, scaled down, land released) · wide range of structures, error-free.
